title: Move suppression for the joint controller: switching, energy cost, and time-step sensitivity
research_question: Can a switching threshold make the joint controller's results insensitive to the simulation time step (E004 failed at 0.52%) without costing energy?
hypothesis: H1: thresholds up to 5% cut the number of action changes by less than 25%, because most switching tracks demand rather than chatters. H2: at a 2% threshold the worst per-seed change in grid energy between dt = 1 s and dt = 0.5 s falls below 0.5% in both scenarios. H3: a 2% threshold costs at most 0.3% energy per successful task versus no threshold.
null_hypothesis: Suppression neither reduces time-step sensitivity nor is cheap.
evaluation_criteria: H1 on seed-mean action changes; H2 on max over seeds of |E(dt=1)/E(dt=0.5) - 1| within each threshold; H3 paired CI of energy per successful task.
known_limitations: Threshold acts on predicted, not measured, savings.
disclosure: Before registration one exploratory run (S1, seed 4, dt 1 s) showed action changes falling from 102 to 89 at a 5% threshold, with all switching in clocks and flow and none in supply temperature. H1 was written after seeing that run. No dt comparison with suppression was run.
data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
